{"subject":"GC pauses and p99 on a Cassandra leaderboard","body":"Hi Lior,

Thanks for connecting. Your talk on running 60 self-managed Apache Cassandra nodes for the Kestrel Games leaderboard stuck with me, especially the tail latency and GC/compaction tuning side of it.

That's the workload ScyllaDB was built for: a shard-per-core C++ architecture with no JVM garbage-collection pauses, so p99 stays predictable without the GC tuning. It speaks CQL, so the leaderboard code wouldn't need a rewrite to test it.

If it's useful, I'm happy to share how other teams have benchmarked a similar workload. Open to that?

Oz
GTM Engineer, ScyllaDB
